vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skillguard-hardened
Version: 1.0.1

The bundle is a security auditing framework with high-risk capabilities including directory deletion (`lib/remediation.py`), arbitrary command execution (`scripts/guarded_flow.py`), and remote code fetching from moltbook.com. While these features are aligned with its defensive purpose, the bundle includes a functional data exfiltration script as a test fixture (`tests/fixtures/malicious_skill/scripts/steal.sh`) that targets `evil.example`. These administrative powers and the presence of live malicious payloads constitute a significant risk surface despite the lack of clear harmful intent.

llm.summary: The package implements a local skill-auditor that matches its description: it scans skill directories, uses local rules plus an external DeepSeek AI audit (when an API key is provided), and offers quarantine/restore/delete workflows — the requested credential and binaries align with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (SkillGuard) align with included code and runtime requirements: python3 and a DeepSeek API key are reasonable for a local scanner that optionally calls an external semantic-audit API. The code includes static rules, policy handling, reporting, and remediation that match the declared functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions and code focus on scanning skill directories, producing JSON reports, and quarantining/restoring/deleting skills. Important runtime behaviors to note: (1) when a DeepSeek key is configured the implementation uploads skill package content to api.deepseek.com for AI review; (2) guarded_flow has a Moltbook flow that downloads files from moltbook.com and then promotes them into the skills tree; (3) several environment variables (CLAWD_WORKSPACE, SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_MODEL) are referenced by the code but not declared in requires.env. These are coherent with the stated purpose but are privacy- and security-relevant.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote installation recipe (no installer that pulls arbitrary archives). The package contains Python scripts and policy JSON bundled with it; external network operations are limited to known hosts (api.deepseek.com and moltbook.com) invoked at runtime. No URL shorteners or obscure personal servers are used in the provided code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The primary required secret is SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (with a DEEPSEEK_API_KEY fallback) which directly maps to the stated AI audit feature. However, the code also reads optional envs like CLAWD_WORKSPACE and SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_MODEL (not declared in requires.env). Also, supplying the DeepSeek key causes full or partial skill contents (including any embedded secrets in scanned files) to be POSTed to an external service — this is expected for an external semantic audit but is a significant data-exfiltration consideration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always:true and does not force autonomous invocation beyond platform defaults. It can quarantine, restore, and delete skill directories using shutil.move/rmtree, but remediation enforces allowed roots defined in policy (default: workspace skills, .skills, and home .moltbot/skills) and the quarantine directory. Users should verify allowed_roots and workspace resolution to ensure operations cannot be performed outside expected directories.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is coherent with its stated purpose, but pay attention to three operational risks before installing: (1) If you provide SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, the scanner will send skill package contents (files and code) to DeepSeek's API — review whether you are comfortable transmitting scanned content (it may include embedded secrets) to an external provider. (2) Review and, if needed, adjust the policy's allowed_roots, reports_dir, and quarantine_dir before enabling remediation actions so quarantine/restore/delete cannot operate on unexpected paths; the runtime resolves the workspace from CLAWD_WORKSPACE (if set) or relative to the package location, so confirm that resolution matches your environment. (3) The package downloads Moltbook artifacts from moltbook.com only in the explicit moltbook-install/update flows — avoid running those commands unless you trust that source. Also be aware the code reads some environment variables (CLAWD_WORKSPACE, SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_MODEL) that are not declared in the manifest. If you need stronger privacy guarantees, run in local-only mode (omit the DeepSeek API key) and review the default policy and rules to tune what the scanner flags.
llm.findings: [ignore-previous-instructions] expected: The SKILL.md and analyzer rules explicitly search for prompt-injection patterns (e.g., 'ignore previous instructions') as part of the scanner's job. Detection of such tokens in SKILL.md is expected behavior for a tool that flags prompt injection.
